The earlier answer was wrong: `(?<!^)(?=[A-Z])` splits every capital, so an acronym like `PHP` becomes `P H P`. The fix inserts a space only at a lowercase-to-uppercase boundary. I ran it against `"Python"`, `"PythonProgrammingExamples"` and `"GetStartedWithPHP"`, and all three pass.

The team note's two options don't fit this task. Option 1 returns `" Python"` with a leading space, which fails the `"Python"` assert. Option 2 doesn't insert spaces between words, and `capitalize()` would turn `"GetStartedWithPHP"` into `"Getstartedwithphp"`. So I've used neither.

```python
import re

def capital_words_spaces(s):
    return re.sub(r'(?<=[a-z])(?=[A-Z])', ' ', s)
```
